audits.published_statement: As read: projecting the Einstein equation once along the normal and once along the slice gives the momentum constraint 8 pi J_i = [div_g(k - (tr k) g)]_i, where J_i = h^b_i n^a T_ab is the momentum density seen by observers at rest in the slices (2409.07639 eq.2.4b, Maxwell term dropped). A t = const slice of a static metric is time-symmetric data, k = 0 (2409.07639 p.15, for its metric), and time-symmetric data have P = 0 (1110.2087 p.2). So for ds^2 = -N^2 dt^2 + h_ij dx^i dx^j with N and h independent of t, J = 0 and T^{0i} = -E beta^i/N^2 + J^i/N = 0 (beta = 0, J = 0) in these coordinates. Equivalently G_{0i} = R_{0i} = 0 identically (re-derived, check B). No source read here states a converse of the form 'a shift vector forces T^{0i} != 0'. Le 2602.18023 Lemma 2 says the opposite for gradient and rigid-rotation shifts.
published_hypotheses: Static: a timelike Killing field that is orthogonal to the t-slices, so coordinates exist with g_{0i} = 0 and every g_ab independent of t (restated as time-symmetric slices, k = 0).
T^{0i} = 0 is a statement about components in those static-adapted coordinates: J_i is defined relative to the normal n of the t-slices.
Einstein's equation G_ab (+ Lambda g_ab) = 8 pi T_ab carries k = 0 over to J = 0. Lambda g_{0i} = 0, so a cosmological constant changes nothing.
The metric is regular enough to define curvature (C^2 in the classical statement).

No source asserts a converse. For a metric with a shift, J vanishes exactly for gradient-plus-rigid-rotation shifts, on smooth R^3 with bounded vorticity and on flat, unit-lapse, time-independent slices (Le 2602.18023 Lemma 2).
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED, the adapted coordinates. phase1.py:90-94 says 'G^{0i} = 0, hence T^{0i} = 0' for 'any static Phi', and D4 (i) (specthm.py:1263-1265; ledger.py:1270ff M-D64-1) is a component condition that names no frame. The theorem holds only in static-adapted coordinates. Check D5 takes the same static isotropic geometry and writes it in Galilean-moving coordinates X = x - v t: T^{0x} = v T^{00} = -6.44e-4, not zero. This does no harm to phase1's own ansatz, which uses adapted coordinates (transition.py:155-158), but as a component statement D4 depends on the choice of coordinates.

ADDED, the converse. The tree says 'it fails automatically for anything with a shift vector' (phase1.py:93-94), 'impossible with a shift vector' (phase1.py:535) and 'The shift vector gives T^{0i} != 0' (phase1.py:255). No source states this, and counterexamples show it is false in general. D1 is flat space with a constant shift, D2 flat space with a rigid-rotation shift, and D3 Kerr, a genuinely non-static vacuum with g_{t phi} = -160/901 at (M, a, r, cos th) = (1, 1/2, 5, 1/3). audits.lacked_data: The tree uses Plummer's pair as an exact solution of Poisson's equation, a smoothing kernel. It does not use Plummer's empirical fit to globular-cluster star counts. The identity contains no measured quantity: sympy re-derives it from grad^2 Phi = 4 pi rho and the formula alone. So no datum Plummer lacked in 1911 can move it, and this is evidence against M's hypothesis for this result. Where the tree goes beyond Plummer's regime, the cause is a change of hypothesis, not missing data: negative mass; strong field (Phi_max = 0.25 at the design point, up to about 4 in the header rows, where the model metric degenerates at the core centre); and infinite extent described as 'compact'. Each is listed as drift with its site.
audits.grade_evidence: The result as used, 'a Plummer-smoothed core of mass -m' (concentric.py:44-46, 167), is re-derived exactly with sympy: its Poisson density is the Plummer profile with total mass exactly -m, and the monopoles cancel exactly against the shell. The restated published pair agrees in form, sign and normalisation. Each hypothesis the tree changes is either named by the owner (lines 122-133, 139-143, 145-147) or shown here not to move what rests on it. Infinite extent puts 1.5e-8 of the mass outside R_s and M_ADM is still 0. The metric degenerates only for m >= 2e-2, and specthm's mu = 5e-3 and 0.6 mu are below that. No datum enters. Three discrepancies are recorded and not repaired; none is a refutation: (1) the header's M_ADM figures at lines 50-51 are a = 0.5 values; (2) the selftest pin at line 268 is the a = 0 value and passes by 3e-10; (3) the header's trace ratio of 7.55e-4 is a finite-difference value 1.2 % below the exact 7.64e-4. Caveat: Plummer 1911 itself is NAMED-NOT-READ, and the restatement read is a code library rather than an arXiv review. STANDS rests on the computed mathematics, which needs no source; only the attribution rests on the restatement. Later literature was not searched (quota).

verifiers.reason:
I could not refute STANDS in either direction. Three points need correcting, and none of them moves the grade.

WHAT I CHECKED
(1) Source, now READ at source. alphaXiv answered this time. Dehnen 2001, astro-ph/0011568, eq. (30) on p.9 restates "the Plummer (1911) sphere" as rho = 3M r_s^2 / (4 pi (r_s^2+r^2)^(5/2)) and Phi = -GM/sqrt(r_s^2+r^2), with the reference "Plummer H.C., 1911, MNRAS, 71, 460". Table 1 (p.6) gives the same kernel, density (3/4pi)(1+r^2)^(-5/2) with phi = 1/sqrt(1+r^2). This agrees with galpy and with the auditor's sympy pair term for term. So the attribution now rests on an arXiv restatement, which is the route the docket asks for. Plummer 1911 itself stays NAMED-NOT-READ. Dehnen also states, in §3.2.2 and §3.3.1, that Plummer softening "is non-compact ... gravity is modified not only at small distances, but on all scales". That supports the audit's 'COMPACT' drift note. The audit's Dehnen row, marked NAMED-NOT-READ with the expected relation 'extends', can now be marked READ. Nothing in Dehnen bears on the grade.

(2) Re-derivation. The auditor's script exits 0. I checked by hand: Phi(1) = 4.97400e-3 at a = 0.02; the a = 0 value is 4.975e-3; the a = 0.5 pair is +4.4471e-3 and -6.25e-13; the a = 0.02 tail is -1.0e-15; the fraction outside R_s is 1.5e-8. specthm.py:524 computes plummer_outside from the same enclosed-mass formula, 1-(1+(a/R_s)^2)^-1.5, which is consistent.

(3) The finite-difference attribution is confirmed. I ran the owner's trace_ratio with composite's step H varied by patching function defaults read-only. It gives 6.153e-4, 7.268e-4, 7.547e-4, 7.616e-4 and 7.633e-4 at H = 4e-3 down to 2.5e-4. That converges as H^2 to about 7.639e-4, the auditor's exact sympy value. So the printed 7.55e-4 is truncation, as the audit says.

(4) Hypothesis drift. The ray at b = 1 never enters r < 0.16, where the linearised metric degenerates. Everything resting on the result needs only Phi at r >~ 1 (Phi ~ m, weak there) and the 1/r coefficient. The M_ADM = 0 claim is read off the given metric's far field. certify.py's seated m = 2e-2 = a, which specthm cites as a 'Plummer core', uses an exponential conformastatic metric (certify.py:203-213). That metric is Lorentzian everywhere, so the degeneracy does not reach it. That use is also outside the canonical rests_on_it.

CORRECTIONS (recorded, not grade-moving)
(a) The audit's closed form 'ratio ~ 2(a/b)^2' holds only at linear order in m. Exact symbolic tidal matrix at m = 5e-3, b = 1, same contraction k = (1,1,0,0):

| a | exact ratio | 2a^2/(a^2+b^2) |
|---|---|---|
| 0.02 | 7.640e-4 | 7.997e-4 |
| 0.01 | 1.663e-4 | 2.000e-4 |
| 0.005 | 1.677e-5 | 5.000e-5 |
| 0 | 3.306e-5 | 0 |

There is an O(m^2) floor from the linearised metric not being a vacuum solution at second order. So the 'b/a >~ 50' rule has that closed form only while 2(a/b)^2 >> ~m^2 effects. The audit's own 4.5 % linear-versus-exact gap at a = 0.02 already shows this.

(b) The audit's what_would_change says the grade moves to NARROWED 'if something resting on this result were shown to use the core at m >~ a/2'. The owner's report VERDICT, which is listed in rests_on_it, does quote the window '5e-3 to 4e-2' and the best lead at m = 2e-2, both in the degenerate-centre regime. It uses those m values only along the b = 1 ray, never the core interior. The audit already says this at the drift item, so the trigger is met in wording but not in substance. (c) The citation 'concentric.py:139-143' for the weak-field admission runs into item 3 (astigmatic focus). The admission itself is lines 139-141.

None of these reaches the Poisson identity, which is closed-form and machine-checked. Nor do they reach the sign-symmetric use with mass -m, which is a named change of hypothesis, or anything that rests on the result.

verifiers.reason:
The audit is not refuted, and STANDS is the grade the evidence supports for the Plummer pair as the tree uses it.

RE-RUN. I copied the script to verify/rederive/plummer-potential.py and ran it. It exits 0 and every printed number matches the audit:
- 1.50000e-8 of the core mass lies outside R_s.
- Phi(1) = 4.97400e-3 and Phi(1000) = -1.0000e-15 at the design point.
- The header pair matches a = 0.5, R_s = 200: +4.4471e-3 and -6.2500e-13.
- The selftest pin is off by 9.997e-7, inside its tolerance by 3.0e-10.
- The exact trace ratios are 3.9902e-1, 1.9704e-2 and 7.6397e-4. The owner's live values are 3.9902e-1, 1.9695e-2 and 7.5468e-4.
- At linear order the trace is 6ma^2/(a^2+b^2)^(5/2) and the ratio is 2a^2/(a^2+b^2).

ENCODING. Section A is the theorem itself, not a toy. It takes the exact symbolic Laplacian of m/sqrt(r^2+a^2), the exact enclosed-mass integral and the limit of the total mass. I confirmed the published side by reading galpy 1.12.0 PlummerPotential.py, whose md5 9ce3712337920ed87880d0574cd0b23a matches the audit. Its terms are Phi = -amp/sqrt(R^2+z^2+b^2), dens = 3/(4pi) b^2 (r^2+b^2)^(-5/2) and mass = (1+b^2/r^2)^(-3/2). These are the same pair with M -> -m.

The section D tidal check uses the owner's own definition, composite.tidal with k = (1,1,0,0). That k is not null in the exact metric, so this measures the owner's test rather than a pure vacuum test. Even so, it is the correct object to compare against the header. I checked it independently with a 60-digit mpmath copy of composite.tidal (verify/rederive/mpcheck.py), which gives 7.6396613e-4, matching sympy.

The audit says the owner's 7.55e-4 is finite-difference truncation. That is confirmed. I varied composite's step H in fdcheck.py: 6.80e-4 at H = 3e-3, 7.547e-4 at 1e-3, 7.631e-4 at 3e-4 and 7.637e-4 at 1e-4. The error scales as H^2, and roundoff sets in at 3e-5. So the printed 7.55e-4 is a discrepancy, not an error of substance, and the closed-form ratio is linear-order only. In the exact composite metric a point mass (a -> 0) leaves a floor of 3.3e-5 at m = 5e-3, and the deviation from linear order scales as about m^2. The audit's 'ratio ~ 2(a/b)^2' is correctly labelled linear order.

VACUITY. I made mutants of sections A to C (vacuity.py), and every one fails the checks it should:
- A Hernquist core m/(r+a) fails the Poisson, density and enclosed-mass checks. It correctly still passes 'total mass = -m', which Hernquist also satisfies.
- A sign-flipped core fails four checks, including total mass (it gets +m).
- An exponent of -1/3 fails four checks.
- A shell of mass 2m fails the Gauss jump.
- A discontinuous shell fails continuity.
- The error-1 constant-offset potential fails both the no-1/r check and the tail check.
The checks are not vacuous.

FLAGS (recorded, not refutations):
(1) The audit says the header pair 'matches the a = 0.5 configuration described in the file's own error 3'. That is imprecise. Error 3's defaults are a = 0.5 with R_s = 30, which gives Phi(1) = 4.3055e-3 and would print as 4.3e-3. The header pair is the a = 0.5, R_s = 200 value, which the audit also states correctly elsewhere.
(2) The audit's what_would_change says the grade moves to NARROWED 'if something resting on this result were shown to use the core at m >~ a/2'. One item in its own rests_on_it already does: concentric.report's VERDICT prints the constants 'window runs 5e-3 to 4e-2' and 'best relative lead -6.0e-4' (from m = 2e-2), taken from header rows 73-74. The model metric's core centre is non-Lorentzian at those m. The grade_evidence names only specthm's mu, which is below that. The report's computed loop stops at m = 1e-2, where g_xx(0) = +1e-4.
This does not touch the Plummer identity, which holds exactly at every m. It belongs to the weak-field hypothesis of the composite metric, already listed as drift. So I keep STANDS for this result. The audit should either reword its NARROWED trigger or carry this item explicitly into the weak-field / linearised-metric audit, which owns it. I made no edits under research/warp-drive.

verifiers.reason:
Every value_then and value_now in the audit reproduces. Two rows need their wording corrected, and one of those corrections is a real finding. Neither moves the grade of the Plummer result.

Checked at source: concentric.py lines 44-46, 50-51, 104-107, 155-167, 182-188 and 268, plus composite.tidal and riemann_lower (lines 172-237). My scripts are separate from the audit's and live in verify/data/: plummer_data_check.py, null_k_check.py and null_k_mscan.py.

Row 1 (Plummer's fit data). Correct. The tree uses only the Poisson identity, so no datum enters.

Row 2 (header M_ADM pair). The values are confirmed. At the design point (m=5e-3, a=0.02, R_s=200), Phi(1) = 4.974000e-3 and Phi(1000) = -1.000e-15. At a=0.5, R_s=200 they are 4.447136e-3 and -6.25e-13. Phi(1000)/Phi(1) does not depend on m: it is -2.01e-13 at a=0.02 against the header's -1.41e-10, so no m gives both header values. One correction: the audit says the pair "matches the a = 0.5 configuration described in the file's own error 3". Error 3's harness defaults are a=0.5 and R_s=30, and that gives Phi(1) = 4.3055e-3, which would print as 4.3e-3, not 4.4e-3. The audit's own script prints this row. The pair matches a=0.5 with R_s=200. Error 3 accounts for the a, not the R_s. moves_conclusion NO follows, since the far field has no 1/r tail at any a.

Row 3 (selftest pin at line 268). Confirmed. The pin 4.9750e-3 is m - m/R_s, the a=0 value. It is off by 9.997e-7, inside the tolerance of 1e-6 by 3e-10.

Row 4 (trace ratio). Every number reproduces. My own sympy Riemann at (0,1,0), using the owner's contraction, gives 3.990185e-1, 1.970411e-2 and 7.639661e-4. The owner's finite-difference value converges to the exact one as h goes to 0, at O(h^2): 7.5468e-4, 7.6163e-4, 7.6334e-4 and 7.6366e-4 at h = 1e-3, 5e-4, 2.5e-4 and 1e-4. So the printed 7.55e-4 is finite-difference truncation, as the audit says.

The finding is this. The audit calls 7.64e-4 the "exact-metric optical tidal matrix" ratio, but it is exact only for the owner's contraction. That contraction uses k = (1,1,0,0), which is not null in the model metric: g(k,k) = -4 Phi. With a properly null k in the same exact metric, the ratio at the design point is 7.32e-3. That is ten times larger and above the owner's 1e-3 criterion. The ratios are 4.037e-1, 2.616e-2 and 7.317e-3 at a = 0.5, 0.1 and 0.02.

An m-scan places the excess. At a=0.02 the null-k ratio is 8.010e-4 at m=1e-6, 2.12e-3 at 1e-3, 7.32e-3 at 5e-3 and 1.36e-2 at 1e-2. In the owner's contraction it stays near 8e-4. Both tend to the linear 2a^2/(a^2+b^2) = 7.997e-4 as m goes to 0, which confirms the audit's closed form. The excess is O(m^2) and comes from the (1+2Phi, 1-2Phi) metric not being an exact vacuum solution outside the core. It does not come from the Plummer density.

So the reason row 4 gives for moves_conclusion NO ("still below the owner's 1e-3 criterion") holds only at linear order or in the owner's non-null contraction. NO still follows for this result, because the Plummer core's contribution to the trace is exactly 6ma^2/(a^2+b^2)^(5/2), a ratio of 8.0e-4 at b/a = 50. The 7.3e-3 belongs to the WEAK FIELD drift. It bears on concentric.report's "traceless to 7.5e-4" verdict, which this audit lists as resting on the result. Because the WEAK FIELD drift row says that drift moves nothing resting on the result apart from the core-centre degeneracy, the finding should be added to that drift row and to row 4's note. It is a discrepancy to record, not an error to repair, and it is not a refutation of the Plummer pair.

audits.name: Gravitational-lens focal length b^2/(4M) (source-at-infinity focus); a source inside it forms no real image

source.located: Textbook weak-field result with no single owning paper. It combines Einstein's deflection alpha = 4GM/(c^2 b) (Ann. Phys. 49 (1916) 769, pre-arXiv), the thin-lens point-mass lens equation (Refsdal 1964, pre-arXiv), the solar-gravitational-lens focal distance b^2/(2 r_g) (Turyshev & Toth, e.g. arXiv:1703.05783), and the Jacobi / optical-tidal-matrix account of conjugate points (Perlick, arXiv:1010.3416). composite.py cites no paper for b^2/4M.
source.via: Not reached at source in this stage. alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries (1703.05783, 1010.3416), get_paper_content(fullText) and discover_papers all returned 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded'. curl to arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org, alphaxiv.org, semanticscholar and r.jina.ai all got CONNECT 403 from the egress proxy. The d67/src cache holds no lensing text. The only external text read is Barcelo & Visser gr-qc/0003025 eq. 5.52 (cached, lines 2429-2432), which restates VLBI gamma = 1 - (0.6 +/- 3.1)e-4; it is used only for the gamma-sensitivity check. The grade rests on a first-principles machine re-derivation, not on a quotation.

audits.published_statement: Not read at source. The textbook form the tree uses was re-derived here, not quoted. A ray passing a mass M at impact parameter b (weak field M << b, thin lens b << distances, G = c = 1) is deflected toward it by alpha = 4M/b. Rays at that b from a source at infinity cross the axis at f = b/alpha = b^2/(4M). For a point source at distance D_s, the rays at that b reconverge at D_i with 1/D_s + 1/D_i = 4M/b^2. D_i is positive (a real caustic or image) only when D_s > b^2/(4M).
published_hypotheses: weak field: |M|/b << 1, with corrections of order M/b
thin lens: b << D_s, D_i
fixed impact parameter b: f depends on b, so the lens has a focal line and 'no real image' refers to the rays at that b
vacuum exterior along the ray: b larger than the lens radius
geometric optics (null geodesics)
PPN gamma = 1 (GR) in alpha = 2(1+gamma)M/b
positive M for the axis-crossing reading; for M < 0 the axisymmetric lens diverges
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED ROUTE for M < 0 (composite.py:290-293; canonical hypothesis 'follows from the 4M/b deflection'). For M < 0 the 4M/b deflection is repulsive and there is no axis-crossing focus. The |M| value is still correct for what composite.py measures (det A = 0 of the thin Jacobi bundle). The integrated tidal matrix is astigmatic: azimuthal power +4M/b^2 (= alpha/b), radial power -4M/b^2 (= -d alpha/db), trace 0. So the focusing power is 4|M|/b^2 for either sign: azimuthal for M > 0, radial for M < 0. The stated derivation route holds only for M > 0.

DROPPED 'fixed b' (composite.py:290-293 docstring 'A source INSIDE this forms no real image'; specthm.py:2373 QUOTES 'forms no real image'). Neither carries 'at this b'. The bare sentence is false for the lens as a whole: the same source at D_s = 5, M = 2e-3, seen through b = 0.15 (f = 2.81) seats at D_i = 5.95 numerically (thin lens gives 6.43). The tree's use is at fixed b = 0.3 (composite.py:122, 384-386), so the use is correct and only the wording drifts.

DROPPED 'to O(M/b)' (composite.py:48-49, 290-293 state b^2/4M as exact). Measured: the effective threshold lies in (11.0, 11.5], not at 11.25. The source-40 conjugate is at 55.87 (Born approximation, both signs) and 55.27 / 56.48 (bent ray), against the thin-lens 55.65. These are corrections of order M/b = 0.0067. They cannot affect the selftest's inside case: D_s = 5 is 6.25 inside f.

DROPPED 'finite run' in the dependent SR1 (specthm.py:1309, 'source outside the focal length (composite.py: a real image forms)'). Being outside f is necessary but not sufficient inside a finite window: the conjugate lies at D_s + f D_s/(D_s - f). For example D_s = 12 gives D_i ~ 180 (thin lens) or 213 (numeric), beyond composite's lam = 75.
KEPT: vacuum along the ray, null congruence, weak field and positive M are all named in SR1 (specthm.py:1309). SR1's positive M is narrower than composite.py's |M|.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (lens-focal-length-b2-over-4m, audited NARROWED)
verifiers.reason:
NARROWED holds. Its strongest support is better than the auditor found, while two of its four stated reasons are weaker than the audit presents them. Several parts of the record need correcting.

(1) THE SOURCES ARE NOW READ AT alphaXiv, so the claim no longer rests on re-derivation alone. Turyshev, arXiv:1703.05783 p.1 prints the deflection as delta = 2 r_g/|b_0| + O(r_g^2) with r_g = 2GM/c^2. That is 4M/b, and the O(M/b) qualifier is stated at the source. The same page says "depending on the impact parameter, the SGL's focus is a semi-infinite line that begins at ~547 AU", which confirms at source that the focal length depends on b. The formula b^2/(2r_g) itself is not printed there. 547 AU is consistent with it: b = R_sun gives 548 AU, computed here. Perlick, arXiv:1010.3416 pp.13-17 gives the optical tidal matrix of eq. (17), Ricci plus a Weyl psi_0 term. There, a zero of one shape parameter is a multiplicity-one caustic (astigmatic, collapsing to a line), and caustic points are conjugate points. That is composite's det A = 0 notion. Both later_literature entries should change from NAMED-NOT-READ to READ, with effect 'agrees'. The 'contested' placeholder should be dropped.

(2) REASON (c), "b^2/4M only to O(M/b)", IS REAL AND STRONGER THAN SHOWN. I ran composite.survey read-only (python -B, same step h = 75/900) with M = +2e-3 and b = 0.3. A source at D_s = 11.15 seats at lambda = 711.5, and one at D_s = 11.2 seats at lambda = 558.75. Both are INSIDE f = 11.25. D_s = 11.0 does not seat. With M = -2e-3, D_s = 11.2 does not seat. So in the tree's own instrument, at the very b the docstring refers to, "a source INSIDE this forms no real image" fails within an O(M/b) band for M > 0. The auditor's own bent-ray numbers imply this too, though the audit never draws it: f_eff = 1/(1/40 + 1/15.273) = 11.05 for M > 0 and 11.67 for M < 0. Composite's printed 55.16 gives 11.00.

The auditor's line "threshold in (11.0, 11.5], not at 11.25" is weak as evidence, because that interval contains 11.25. My independent Born run gives f_eff = 11.36 for both signs. This is a mixed-order quantity: the Jacobi equation is solved exactly over a linearised metric, so the precise offset is not a consistent O(M^2) result. Only its order is meaningful.

The audit's stated WRONG trigger is "a computed weak-field conjugate for D_s < f at the same b". That is now literally met, so the trigger is mis-phrased. It should read "outside the O(M/b) band". The band is about 0.2 against f = 11.25, so this is the NARROWED qualifier, not a refutation. The selftest's D_s = 5 case, which sits 6.25 inside f, is untouched.

(3) REASON (a), "fixed b dropped", IS OVERSTATED. composite.py:48 reads "At b = 0.3, source at 40 (OUTSIDE the focal length b^2/4M -- inside it no real image forms". focal_length (composite.py:290) takes b as an argument. specthm.py:2373 is a substring QUOTES tag, not a claim. The audit says "neither carries 'at this b'", and that is wrong for line 48. What drifts is the canonical name. R4b's b = 0.15 example is correct, but it refutes a reading the owner does not make.

(4) REASON (b), "the M < 0 route", IS DRIFT AGAINST THE CANONICALIZER'S INFERRED HYPOTHESIS, NOT AGAINST composite. composite.py:105 itself names "THE FOCUS IS ASTIGMATIC ... one transverse direction converges while the other diverges: det A = 0 is a LINE focus", and composite.py:102 names "LINEARISED WEAK FIELD". The value b^2/(4|M|) for M < 0 is correct at leading order: the radial power is 4|M|/b^2. My independent RK4 integration of the radial component confirms identical Born conjugates for both signs.

(5) REASON (d), SR1 at specthm.py:1309, STANDS as a narrowing. Outside f is not sufficient within a finite run. At O(M/b) it is not sufficient even at infinite run for M < 0, though SR1 restricts itself to positive M.

No misprint is involved and no datum moves anything. PPN gamma moves f by under 6e-3, as the audit says. The narrowing is correctly a matter of hypotheses: O(M/b) is now evidenced in composite.py's own code, and the SR1 finite window still holds. The fixed-b and M-sign items should be marked as canonical-wording drift, not owner drift. I did not edit anything under research/, and git status of research/ is clean.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: run a copy of the script, check whether its encoding is the theorem or a toy of it, and run vacuity guards with the hypotheses negated.
verifiers.reason:
RE-RUN. I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and ran it with python3 -B and --run-composite. It exits 0, and every printed figure matches the audit: f = 45/4; source 40 conjugate at 55.866 (Born, both signs), 55.273 and 56.479 (bent); source 5 gives none in all four runs; R4b seats at lambda 10.949; R6 moves f by 5.57e-3. composite.selftest() prints SELFTEST OK. git status of research/ is clean.

ENCODING. The script checks the result in the setting where the tree uses it, not a looser toy. That setting is a linearised static metric with Phi = -M/r and a Jacobi matrix with det A = 0, which is exactly the setting composite.py:34-40 states. R1 and R2 are a real symbolic derivation: the tidal matrix, its trace, and the integrated astigmatic powers -4M/b^2 and +4M/b^2. Weak points:
- R3's 'D_i > 0 iff D_s > f' is checked at only two sample points. It is trivially true algebraically, so this is not a flaw.
- R4's 1.5 tolerance only tests f to within about 7% (f = b^2/(4.2M) would pass).
- The sweep's step size (h = 0.033) was not tested for convergence in the script. I tested it: D_i at D_s = 11.5 and 12 is unchanged at h = 0.005.

VACUITY (my own code, adv.py):
- M = 0 gives no conjugate.
- A source inside f gives no conjugate even when run to 4000.
- Flipping the tidal sign still seats, as the astigmatic, sign-blind account predicts.
- At M/b = 0.2, D_i comes out 0.91 against a thin-lens 0.60, so the weak-field hypothesis is load-bearing.

WHERE THE AUDIT OVER-STATES THE CASE AGAINST THE TREE:
(a) 'Dropped fixed b' is weak. focal_length(M, b=B_DEFAULT) carries b in its signature, and SR1's own statement (specthm.py:1317-1323) names f(b), 'only the rays of ONE impact parameter reconverge', and 'a focal line, not a point focus'. The specthm:2373 entry is only a quote-match string.
(b) composite.py never says its M < 0 focal length comes from the deflection. It says Weyl focusing is sign-blind and det A includes shear (lines 27-29, 39-40). That is the astigmatic route the audit itself derives. The drift is against the canonical paraphrase, not against the owner.
(d) SR1 asserts only that a real image forms when the source is outside f. That is true. Nowhere in the SR1 entry I read (specthm.py:1304-1330) does it claim the image forms within a finite run.
(e) '(11.0, 11.5], not at 11.25': that bracket contains 11.25, so it cannot by itself show the threshold is not 11.25.

WHAT THE AUDIT UNDER-STATES. Item (c), O(M/b), is a real narrowing, and stronger than the audit showed.
- Born effective f is 11.360, the same at D_s = 40, 20 and 15. Its offset f_eff/f - 1 scales linearly as about 1.47 M/b across four values of M.
- Born gives no conjugate at D_s = 11.3. The thin lens predicts D_i of about 2542 there, within the 4000 run, so 11.25 is not the threshold.
- On the bent ray at M = +2e-3, a source at D_s = 11.15, INSIDE b^2/4M = 11.25, forms a real conjugate at D_i = 1329.4. This is converged: n = 150k and n = 300k give the same value. Sources at 11.0 and 10.9 give none.
So the bare sentence 'a source INSIDE this forms no real image' (composite.py:291) is false in a sliver of width O(M/b)*f for M > 0. It holds to first order only. It is implied by 'linearised' but never stated.

None of this touches the tree's own numbers. Source 5 is 6.25 inside f.

GRADE. NARROWED is supported, mainly through (c), with (a), (b) and (d) reduced to wording issues or extractor-side issues. The sources are still NAMED-NOT-READ. The grade rests on the machine re-derivation alone, which I reproduced.

verifiers.lens: THE DATA CLAIM: every data_at_publication row and the lacked_data answer, checked at source.
verifiers.reason:
The data claim mostly holds, and NARROWED stands. There is one stale value and one unnamed limit on what the data covers. Neither moves the conclusion.

ROW 1 (b, M -> f), correct. f = 0.09/0.008 = 45/4 = 11.25 exactly, with b = 0.3 (B_DEFAULT, composite.py:122). composite.py:384 asserts focal_length(2e-3) = 11.25. Exact arithmetic, so it cannot move.

ROW 2 (inside case), correct. composite.py:385 does run survey(-2e-3, x0 = -5, lam = 60). The thin-lens D_i = 11.25*5/(5 - 11.25) = -9, computed exactly here. The 6.25 margin against corrections of order (M/b)*f ~ 0.075 holds.

ROW 3 (PPN gamma). value_then is correct. The quoted figure is READ: gr-qc/0003025 eq. 5.52 (d67/src cache) gives gamma = 1 - (0.6 +/- 3.1)e-4, a VLBI figure the paper attributes to its ref [38].

DISCREPANCY 1: value_now is stale and mislabelled. That figure is a 2000-era restatement, not the current value. I read Will's review arXiv:1403.7377 at source through alphaXiv; the quota cleared:
- p.40, eq. 59: deflection = (1/2)(1+gamma)*4M/d.
- p.41: VLBI 2004, gamma - 1 = (-1.7 +/- 4.5)e-4.
- p.41: VLBI 2009, gamma - 1 = (-1.6 +/- 1.5)e-4.
- p.43 and Table 4: Cassini 2003, gamma - 1 = (2.1 +/- 2.3)e-5.

f scales as 1/(1+gamma), so the 3-sigma |df/f| bounds are 7.6e-4, 3.05e-4 and 4.5e-5 respectively. These shift f = 11.25 by 8.6e-3, 3.4e-3 and 5.1e-4. moves_conclusion = 'no' therefore follows, and more strongly on the tightest datum (Cassini). One caveat: the 2004 VLBI analysis alone is looser than the figure the audit used.

DISCREPANCY 2, minor rounding: the stated bound '|df/f| <= 4.9e-4' computes to 4.95e-4. The stated shift of 5.6e-3 is consistent with 4.95e-4.

SOURCE CORRECTION: Turyshev arXiv:1703.05783 is now READ at p.1 (the audit had it NAMED-NOT-READ). It gives the deflection delta = 2 r_g/b + O(r_g^2), and says the focus is "a semi-infinite line that begins at ~547 AU", depending on the impact parameter. R_sun^2/(2 r_g) computes to 547.76 AU, which matches. This is a published, read corroboration of the audit's narrowing (a): the focal length holds at fixed b, as a focal line. It also confirms the weak-field qualifier. The paper does not print b^2/(2 r_g) as a formula; that is inferred from the 547 AU figure. The record should change from NAMED-NOT-READ to READ (corroborating).

LACKED_DATA. 'No data gap' is backed by evidence, not presumed: the re-derivation uses no measured input, and gamma is measured. One limit goes unnamed, though. Every gamma datum comes from positive-mass deflection by the Sun at M/b ~ 2.1e-6. The tree uses M/b = 6.7e-3, about 3000 times stronger, and applies |M| to M < 0. No measurement of any kind exists for lensing by a negative mass. The M < 0 branch therefore rests on linearised GR with a negative source alone: it is data-free, not data-confirmed. This should be a named hypothesis, not covered by 'no later datum changes the conclusion'.

M's hypothesis is answered with evidence for this result. GR deflection is now measured to about 2e-5 (Cassini), better than at the audit's own figure, and nothing indicates that earlier physicists lacked data that would change b^2/(4M). The answer is narrower than stated: it holds for M > 0 in the weak field; for M < 0 the result is untested by any data.

Grade: NARROWED is confirmed. WRONG would need a discrepancy beyond the 6.25 margin, and DATA-DEPENDENT would need gamma off by about 1e-2. The data excludes both.

audits.published_statement: v1 pp.16-17, verbatim: 'The analysis in this paper was restricted to a flat spacetime background. In this case, the expectation values of quartic operators which appear in the dimensionless measure of the fluctuations, Delta, or in the Langevin equation, Eq.(4.27), may be defined in terms of normal ordered products. The generalization of this analysis to curved spacetime backgrounds will require a renormalization procedure for quartic operator products in such spacetimes, which has not yet been developed. Note that an alternative approach to fluctuations is to discuss only averaged quantities. If we were to average fields over finite space or time intervals, then we could define a quantity similar to Delta without invoking normal ordering. This approach is used by Barton [10] in his treatment of the fluctuations of the Casimir force. In the present context, this procedure suffers from the defect that it introduces an arbitrary length or time scale into the problem. If, for example, one wished to obtain an equation of the form of Eq.(4.3) using averaged rather than normal-ordered quantities, there would be an inherent ambiguity in the resulting equation.' Reference [10] is G. Barton, J. Phys. A 24, 991 & 5533 (1991). Eq.(4.3) is the Langevin mean-squared velocity <v^2> = m^-2 double-integral [F_c F_c + <F(t1)F(t2)>].
published_hypotheses: H1 'In the present context': a flat (Minkowski) background, a free scalar field, the paper's Delta of Eq.(3.2), and the Langevin description of Sec. IV (Eqs. 4.1-4.3, 4.27).
H2 The averaged alternative is defined 'without invoking normal ordering'. Its purpose is to avoid the Minkowski normal ordering KF use, which does not carry over to curved space.
H3 Fields are averaged 'over finite space or time intervals' with an unspecified window. The scale is 'arbitrary' in the sense that nothing in the field theory fixes it.

H4 The stated consequence is an 'inherent ambiguity' in an equation of the form (4.3). The paper states no theorem and gives no computation of how any averaged quantity depends on the scale. It is a qualitative remark.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (context qualifier): the tree quotes the clause 'introduces an arbitrary length or time scale' (fluctuation.py:110-111) without KF's 'In the present context' (H1) and without the consequence KF draw from it, an 'inherent ambiguity' in an equation of the form (4.3) (H4). The quoted words are a verbatim substring of v1 p.17, checked against line 3029 of the saved text layer. The drop does not change what the tree uses the clause for, which is only that averaging brings in a scale, so it moves nothing. It is named here, not graded down.

REPRESENTATION RISK (not a misquote): KF present averaging as an ALTERNATIVE THEY DECLINE, and call the scale its 'defect'. The tree puts 'KF say so themselves' (fluctuation.py:110) in its list of reasons why the POINTWISE Delta cannot be the demand row (fluctuation.py:105-116), right after '(a) ... the physical quantity is smeared, not pointwise' (fluctuation.py:107-109). A reader could take 'say so themselves' to mean KF endorse smearing. They do not; all KF say is that averaging introduces a scale. The tree's next words, 'AND FOR THE CORRIDOR THE SCALE IS NOT ARBITRARY', do treat the remark as an objection to be answered, which is the faithful reading.

ADDED BY THE TREE (not KF's claim; named so it is not attributed to them): 'FOR THE CORRIDOR THE SCALE IS NOT ARBITRARY. It has its own: the width b, and Fewster's sampling time' (fluctuation.py:111-112). These are two scales, not one. The tree's own successor, noise.py:180-193, shows the sampling time is a RANGE rather than a single value. At b = 1 m, tau = b/c is 61 times the curvature length l_G that the demand sets. That breaks Ford-Roman's condition, 'sampling time ... much smaller than the smallest local radius of curvature' (gr-qc/9607003 Sec. 4). noise.py therefore shortens it to eps*l_G with eps left free; at eps = 1 and 0.1 the shortfall is 64.108 and 60.108 orders. Pfenning's thesis says the same: 'tau_0 is an arbitrary sampling time' (gr-qc/9805037, cached text line 665), restricted only to be smaller than the local radius of curvature. So the tree's rebuttal cuts KF's 'arbitrary' down to 'bounded above by the geometry'. The refusal it supports (PRICES_THE_CORRIDOR = False, fluctuation.py:157) holds across that whole range. This is a finding about the tree's addition, not about KF.

WEAKENED IN THE SUCCESSOR (named): KF define the averaged alternative WITHOUT normal ordering (H2). noise.py:100 smears 'Kuo-Ford's own measure (normal-ordered square, their normalisation)', so it keeps the Minkowski normal ordering the averaged route was meant to avoid. The tree does not hide this. noise.py:145 and 621 also compute the FULL (un-normal-ordered) noise-kernel relative variance, and noise.py:1153 records 'Kuo-Ford <:A^2:> needs a reference state in curved space; Var does not'. audits.lacked_data: The tree cites no source, so 'the authors' here are the GCE modellers whose conclusion it extrapolates. What they lacked was stellar phosphorus: P I lines are weak near-IR/UV features, and by 2020 only ~100 FGKM stars had measured P. Surveys of 163 stars (2022) and ~750 stars (2026) followed. On snippet evidence, which was NOT READ, the new data cut both ways. For M's hypothesis: GCE models underpredict P, so the nucleosynthesis accounting the tree credits is incomplete, and P-rich outliers exist. Against it mattering here: P is observed across the measured disk population, and the tree's finding does not rest on the GCE model at all. z3 check C2 shows the finding needs only one destination holding unshipped stock, and solar-system CI chondrites (sibling-audited) supply that for any trip within the solar system. C3/C4 show that a destination 1 dex poorer in P costs 7.5 t per 70 kg, still 23.8 orders below the Fuchs shell. So the moved data change the figure and the 'every' universal, not the conclusion. No snippet claim is verified here.
audits.grade_evidence: The external result (GCE placing C, N and P in EVERY enriched system, with a CI-like, accessible primitive body there) is uncited in the tree and could not be read at source: alphaXiv quota was exceeded on every call, and arXiv, IOP, OSTI, NSF-PAR and A&A were egress-blocked. Under the docket rule an uncheckable claim is OPEN, not STANDS and not WRONG. What WAS computed limits what hangs on it. (1) The tree's 10.70 reproduces exactly (C1). (2) z3 shows the finding it supports, that 'and that had to travel' is NOT ESTABLISHED (stock.py:124-138), needs only ONE stocked, unshipped destination; 'every' is strictly stronger than needed (C2, vacuity-guarded). So the finding does not inherit the universal's openness. (3) The figure is data-dependent on destination P (10.70*10^(-D), binder flip at D = +0.122) and on CI P and N (sibling audits), and no tested value moves the verdict. Named drifts: the CI-like-body hypothesis is added beyond GCE; 'every' extrapolates population trends; 'from the origin' is an interpretive reading, and on GCE's own mechanism the atoms did travel through the ISM. Pointer discrepancy: CLAIMS.md 4629 is now 4648. Snippet evidence (models underpredict P; per-star scatter) is NAMED-NOT-READ and is not used for the grade. Nothing here shows GCE or the tree's sentence to be wrong.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: Read arXiv:2206.03528, 2009.00009 and 2008.04660 at source once alphaXiv quota resets or egress allows. If they confirm P detected across the measured enriched FGK population, with scatter of a few tenths of a dex and models underpredicting it, the grade becomes NARROWED: 'every enriched system' and 'GCE placed' would hold only as 'observed present in the measured disk population, with per-system scatter and incomplete model accounting', and the CI-like-body hypothesis stays added. Reading Ryugu/Bennu bulk P and white-dwarf P detections would test the added hypothesis. No reading can make the finding WRONG while one stocked, unshipped destination exists (C2).

The audit graded OPEN only because nothing could be read: alphaXiv quota was exceeded and egress was blocked. That no longer holds. I read all three candidate sources at source through alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2026-10-02. The audit's own what_would_change_the_grade says NARROWED once these confirm three things: P detected across the measured enriched FGK population, scatter of a few tenths of a dex, and models underpredicting P. They confirm it.

READ, Maas et al. 2022 (arXiv:2206.03528):
- p1 abstract: 163 FGK stars over -1.09<[Fe/H]<0.47; "chemical evolution models generally under-predict P over the observed metallicity range"; [P/Fe] differs by ~0.1 dex between thin and thick disk (p11: 0.11 dex, above 2-sigma but "not significant at the 3σ level"); P mainly from core-collapse supernovae.
- p2: only ~190 stellar P abundances in all prior surveys combined. APOGEE reports P for tens of thousands of stars, but P is its most uncertain element.
- p13: one GSE halo star sits 0.3-0.5 dex low. P-rich stars exist.
- Selection bias: the sample was chosen so P was detectable (Teff>4500 K, [Fe/H] above about -1.3). It cannot test 'every'.

READ, Hinkel et al. 2020 (arXiv:2009.00009):
- Abstract and p2: P exists for only ~1% of stars (100 in Hypatia). Typical [P/Fe] error is 0.11 dex.
- p4: C, N and P show "real and substantial variations" between stars.
- p6: the Sun is relatively P-rich. Its C/P and N/P are a factor ~2 below the Hypatia average.
- p7: "not possible to outline a plausible range or generalization of P abundances within nearby stars".
- p7-8: P partitions into rocky cores, so surface P is not guaranteed.

READ, Kobayashi, Karakas & Lugaro 2020 (arXiv:2008.04660):
- p1-2: elements with A>=12 are made in stars, and each next generation forms from gas carrying earlier ejecta. This reads the tree's mechanism as standard GCE.
- p20: the predicted [P/Fe] is "in reasonably good agreement" with observations, though "it would be better if P yields increase". So 'models underpredict P' depends on the model. Maas tested Cescutti 2012, Prantzos 2018 and Ritter 2018, not K20. The audit's drift wording "GCE models UNDERPREDICT P" overgeneralizes slightly. This is a wording discrepancy, not a refutation.
- p30: 49% of C and 74% of N come from AGB stars.

Verdict on the external result as the tree uses it (stock.py:129-130):
- The mechanism stands: enriched systems inherit C, N and P from stellar ejecta.
- 'Every enriched star system' is not observed: P is measured in ~1% of catalogued stars, with substantial intrinsic scatter.
- 'GCE placed' is model-incomplete for at least the models Maas tested.
- The CI-like accessible body is an added hypothesis. Hinkel's core-partitioning point bears against assuming it.
That is NARROWED, not WRONG, and not OPEN.

New datum, computed (verify/refute/gce_check.py), in the direction that flatters the tree. stock.CHONDRITE gives every destination solar-CI P, but the Sun is P-rich. Treat the Hypatia-average offset of -0.23 to -0.25 dex (READ, Hinkel Table 1) as D. Then the factor is 18.3-19.2 (1.28-1.34 t per 70 kg), against the tree's 10.70. P still binds, since D* = +0.122. The audit's dropped-metallicity-qualifier drift should name this solar-P-rich bias explicitly. It changes the figure, not the finding.

Minor discrepancies:
- The audit's lacked_data says "by 2020 only ~100 FGKM stars had measured P". That is 100 in Hypatia; Maas counts ~190 across surveys, excluding APOGEE.
- 2609.20930, 2008.01633 and 2309.06467 remain unread by me.

- C2's point stands: the stock.py finding needs only one stocked, unshipped destination, so the narrowing does not reach the finding.

(b) Encoding: C2 is a propositional toy of the finding's logical shape, not of GCE. THE SNIPPETS, NOW READ. All of them hold, with these corrections.
(1) Maas+22, p.1, Table 5 and p.11: 163 FGK stars over -1.09<[Fe/H]<0.47. The words 'models generally under-predict P' are verbatim. The thin/thick offset is 0.11 dex, above 2 sigma but below 3 sigma, over -0.57<[Fe/H]<-0.13. P comes from CCSNe. The best model (Cescutti 2012) needs its massive-star P yields multiplied by 2.75 (p.15).
(2) Gakis+26 confirms the trend on 755 stars. The thick-thin offset is 0.08 dex, not 0.1. At fixed [Fe/H], [P/Fe] spans 'several tenths of a dex', well above the 0.048 median error, and some stars give upper limits only. 'Current prescriptions ... underpredict the absolute P abundance level.' Masseron 2020 and Brauner 2023 found P-rich stars with [P/Fe] above +0.8 to +1.2; this was READ as Gakis restates it, and Masseron itself remains title-only.
(3) Hinkel+20, abstract and pp.2-3: 100 P abundances in Hypatia, about 1% of stars. The audit's 'FGKM' is the catalogue's scope; there are ZERO M stars (64 G, 33 F, 3 K). Maas+22 p.2 counts about 190 across the literature, plus tens of thousands of low-reliability APOGEE values. The audit's 'only ~100 by 2020' therefore holds for Hypatia, not for the literature as a whole.
(4) The audit quotes '~0.11 dex per-star error'. That is Hinkel's 2020 compilation figure; later per-star errors are about 0.05 dex. This does not matter here.
(5) THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS: the audit says 'GCE models underpredict P' as if it held for models in general. It is model-specific. KKL20 p.20 (READ), the tree's likeliest source, says its predicted [P/Fe] is 'in reasonably good agreement with the observations', but it was compared only with Caffau 2011/2016 and Roederer 2014. Maas+22 tested Cescutti, Prantzos and Ritter, not KKL20, and reports that Kobayashi+11 predicts the ~0.1 dex thin/thick offset that is observed. The row should read: models tuned before the 2022-2026 surveys underpredict P, or need ad hoc yield boosts of 2-3x; KKL20 claims agreement against the sparse pre-2020 data.

M'S HYPOTHESIS, answered with READ evidence. The modellers did lack data: KKL20 was compared against roughly 20-40 stars. The 163-star and 755-star surveys showed the model accounting incomplete in level and in shape. So for 'GCE placed' as a MODEL claim, M is right. Against it mattering: the same data observe P throughout the measured disk FGK population. The finding rests on presence, not on the model, and C2 shows one stocked destination is enough.

DATA-ROW CAVEATS.
- Row 3's binder flip at D > +0.122 holds only if N is held at solar CI. That hypothesis is named in C3's output but not in the row. If N scales with metallicity too, metallicity alone does not flip the binder.
- Hinkel p.6 finds the Sun relatively P-rich (C/P and N/P a factor of 2 below the Hypatia mean). Typical hosts therefore lean toward D < 0, away from the flip.
- Measured disk [P/H] reaches about -0.6 at [Fe/H] = -1, so D = -1 is a conservative bound.

GRADE. OPEN rested only on the failure to read. The audit's own what_would_change_the_grade is now met at source: P is detected across the measured FGK disk, with real scatter of several tenths of a dex, models underpredict it, P-rich and P-poor outliers exist, and Hinkel says no plausible range for nearby stars can yet be outlined. On that test the grade becomes NARROWED. 'Every enriched system' narrows to 'observed in the measured disk FGK population, with per-star scatter and upper limits'. 'GCE placed' narrows to 'nucleosynthesis supplies P; model accounting is incomplete'. The CI-like-body hypothesis (arXiv:2309.06467) is still NAMED-NOT-READ. It is a drift the tree added beyond GCE and does not bear on the grade of GCE itself. Nothing read shows the tree's finding to be WRONG. audits.published_statement:
CODATA 2018 and 2022 recommended values, as given in the NIST tables:
- c = 299 792 458 m s^-1, exact.
- G = 6.674 30(15) x 10^-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2, u_r = 2.2e-5, identical in 2018 and 2022.
- g_n = 9.806 65 m s^-2, exact; a conventional standard acceleration of gravity.

IAU 2012 B2: au = 149 597 870 700 m exactly.

IAU 2015 B3: the nominal solar mass parameter GM_sun = 1.3271244 x 10^20 m^3 s^-2 is an exact conversion constant. The solar mass in kg is not a nominal constant. It is GM_sun/G and carries G's uncertainty.
published_hypotheses: c and g_n are exact by definition. c fixes the metre (since 1983); g_n is a conventional value, not a measured local gravity.
au is exact by definition (IAU 2012 B2), not a measured Earth-Sun distance.

G is a least-squares-adjusted measured value with standard uncertainty 0.00015e-11 (u_r 2.2e-5). The input G data are mutually inconsistent and CODATA applies an expansion factor to them. The factor itself is NAMED-NOT-READ here; a web-search snippet of the CODATA 2022 text gives 3.9 over 16 input data, not read at source.
M_sun in kg is DERIVED as nominal GM_sun / G. Its kg value is therefore tied to whichever G is used and carries G's u_r; only GM_sun is known to about 1e-10.

audits.lacked_data:
M's hypothesis, tested for this result.

What the earlier physicists lacked: G is the least well known constant CODATA recommends (u_r 2.2e-5), and its input measurements disagree by more than their stated uncertainties. The recommended values read here are 6.67428 (2006), 6.67384 (2010), 6.67408 (2014) and 6.67430 (2018, 2022). That is a spread of 6.9e-5, and the 2010 value sits 3.1 sigma(2018) below the 2018 value. So "previous physicists lacked data" is literally true of G. It is why the recommended value moved at each of the three adjustments 2006-2010, 2010-2014 and 2014-2018; it did not change 2018-2022.

Would more data change wall.py's conclusion? Computed evidence says no. wall.py's figures depend on G at most as G^1. Several do not depend on G at all: the 14-orders inversion, the AU radii, the areal density, and the Msun figures when M_sun is taken consistently as GM_sun/G. A +-1000 ppm move in G is about 14 times the whole 2006-2022 spread and about 45 times u_r, and it leaves every conclusion and every order of magnitude in place.

The other four inputs lack nothing. c, g_n and the au are definitions, and GM_sun is known to about 1e-10.

The one datum wall.py is behind on is its own M_sun. 1.98847e30 is the pre-2019 value, derived from G(2014). Pairing it with the 2018 G shifts the Msun figures by 3.0e-5. This is recorded as a discrepancy; it changes no printed digit.

Context outside this entry's owner, recorded but not graded: shipspec.py:26, kerr.py:40 and navigate.py:36 use M_sun = 1.98892e30. That equals GM_sun/G only for G = 6.6726e-11, the CODATA-1986-era value, so it is inconsistent with those files' own G = 6.67430e-11 by 2.6e-4.

source.located: These are textbook atomic-structure scaling laws, not the result of one paper: Bohr and Dirac levels, plus the Fermi-contact hyperfine term with a Casimir-type relativistic factor. The variation-of-constants literature uses them: Prestage-Tjoelker-Maleki 1995; Karshenboim 2000 (physics/0008051); Dzuba-Flambaum-Webb 1999; Flambaum-Tedesco 2006 (nucl-th/0601050). The one source READ is the restatement the tree itself cites: Godun et al., PRL 113, 210801 (2014) = arXiv:1407.0164v2, p.4. It prints the coefficients the laws imply (B_E3 = B_E2 = 0, B_Cs = -1, A_Cs = 2.83) and the condition under which B_Cs = -1 holds. It does not print the formulae themselves.

audits.published_statement:
arXiv:1407.0164v2 p.4 (READ): 'Time variation of alpha and mu is measured via the frequency ratio of two clock transitions r = nu_1/nu_2 using the relation r-dot/r = (A_1 - A_2) alpha-dot/alpha + (B_1 - B_2) mu-dot/mu. The sensitivity coefficients A_i of the relevant atomic transitions are: A_E3 = -5.95 [34], A_E2 = 0.88 [35], and A_Cs = 2.83 [36]. Dependence on mu-dot arises through the nuclear magnetic moment and is negligible for optical transitions (the sensitivity coefficient B_E3 = B_E2 = 0). As the 133Cs nuclear g-factor has negligible sensitivity to changes in the strong interaction [37, 38], an AFM history can also be interpreted to set constraints on mu-dot/mu (B_Cs = -1).'

The formula form is the tree's own (address.py:62). Re-derived here: nu_hf/(c R_inf) = (2/3) alpha^2 g_I g_e (m_e/m_p)(2I+1) at Fermi-contact order.
published_hypotheses: P1 (Godun p.4): linear response in the constants, i.e. nu ~ alpha^A mu^B with everything else fixed, where mu = m_p/m_e.

P2 (Godun p.4): B_opt = 0 is called 'negligible', not zero. Godun names mu entering only through the nuclear magnetic moment. Nuclear mass (recoil) and nuclear size also bring it in; see rederive B and D.
P3 (Godun p.4): B_Cs = -1 holds 'As the 133Cs nuclear g-factor has negligible sensitivity to changes in the strong interaction'. Fixed g_I is a stated CONDITION.
P4 (Godun p.4): the A_i, including A_Cs = 2.83 = 2 + 0.83, are many-body atomic calculations from refs [34]-[36], not measurements.

P5 (re-derived, rederive A): nu/(c R_inf) depends on m_e only through three dimensionless groups: alpha, m_e/M and r_N m_e c/hbar. It is a function of alpha alone only when M -> infinity and r_N -> 0, i.e. a point nucleus of infinite mass.

P6 (re-derived, rederive E): the form alpha^2 (m_e/m_p)^1 g_I^1 is the non-relativistic Fermi-contact term, taken at first order in the nuclear dipole, with infinite nuclear mass. Reduced mass adds a factor (1+m_e/M)^-3. F_rel carries the Z alpha dependence, plus finite-size terms (Breit-Rosenthal, Bohr-Weisskopf).

The audit holds up, with three caveats.

- `dln_X_dln_v` gives 7/9 under H1 and 1 under H2.

**Vacuity guard.** I wrote my own script, hfo-scaling-verifier/hfo_vacuity.py, with output in hfo_vacuity.out. It negates each hypothesis in turn:

- **(a) Dimensional analysis.** With the point-nucleus, infinite-mass hypothesis imposed the nullity is 1, which leaves alpha alone. With nuclear mass M and nuclear radius r_N included it is 3. So check A tells the two cases apart. It is Buckingham's theorem, not a toy.

- **(b) Fermi exponents.** These change when their hypotheses are negated. With reduced mass, B_hf = -0.99837. With the Casimir factor at Z = 55, A = 2.739. So check E is a real derivation from SI constants and is not vacuous.

- **(c) Recoil (check D).** I recomputed it at 60 digits with mpmath. It has an exact closed form: d ln ratio / d ln(m_e/M) = (2/9) alpha^2 (m_e/M). The coefficient comes out as 0.222222.

  - So item 3 rests entirely on the RECALLED Barker-Glover/CODATA term. The audit marks it CONDITIONAL, which is correct.

**Caveat 1: check C cannot fail.** sympy's `E_nl_dirac` takes only (n, l, spin_up, Z, c) and has no mass argument. Infinite nuclear mass is therefore built into the encoding. C confirms that the Dirac energy has the form m_e c^2 F(Z alpha), but it does not test the infinite-mass hypothesis. D is what tests it.

The residual is -5.62e-5, so the check fails at the tolerance the label states and passes at the one coded. This is a slip in the script, not in the physics. I subtracted the recalled Breit, alpha^2-QED and Zemach corrections (all NAMED-NOT-READ), and the residual falls to -3.4e-7. That supports the Fermi form more strongly than the audit claimed.

**Grade.** None of this refutes the external laws under their hypotheses. The three narrowings of use are reproduced, each with the size the audit gives:
- fixed g_I, a condition Godun states that the tree never names
- "+1 EXACTLY", although the tree's own H1 K_alpha is nonzero and `eps_detectable_transported` hard-codes 1
- the conditional recoil-versus-finite-size ordering

audits.published_statement: Carroll gr-qc/9712019 p.223: 'addot/a = -(4 pi G/3)(rho + 3p), (8.35) and (adot/a)^2 = (8 pi G/3) rho - k/a^2. (8.36) Together these are known as the Friedmann equations.' These are obtained from the 00 equation (8.33) and the ij equations (8.34) of R_mu_nu = 8 pi G (T_mu_nu - g T/2). Ellis & van Elst gr-qc/9812046v5 p.22: 'The remaining non-trivial equations are the energy equation (37), the Raychaudhuri equation (29), which now takes the form 3 Sddot/S + (1/2)(mu + 3p) = 0, (106) and the Friedmann equation ... 3R = 2mu - (2/3)Theta^2 = 6k/S^2, (107) where k is a constant. Any two of these equations imply the third if Sdot != 0 (the latter equation being a first integral of the other two).' And p.13: 'when omega_a = 0, the generalised Friedmann equation (55) is an integral of the Raychaudhuri equation (29) and energy equation (37).'
published_hypotheses: General relativity: Einstein field equations with the Levi-Civita connection (Carroll 8.29, 8.32; Ellis-van Elst p.10: 'the twice-contracted Bianchi identities which, by Einstein's field equations (1), imply the conservation equations (2)').
FLRW metric: homogeneous and isotropic, with k a constant (Carroll 8.7, 8.12-8.14; Ellis-van Elst (107)).
Perfect fluid comoving with the cosmic frame: U^mu = (1,0,0,0) and T^mu_nu = diag(-rho,p,p,p) (Carroll 8.15-8.18). Ellis-van Elst allow p = p(mu), a sum of such fluids, or a scalar field.
p = w rho with w constant (Carroll 8.21). This is used only to integrate continuity; the Friedmann pair itself does not need it.
Lambda is equivalent to a w = -1 vacuum fluid with rho = -p = Lambda/(8 pi G) (Carroll 8.29-8.31).

The energy, Raychaudhuri and Friedmann equations are not independent: 'any two imply the third if Sdot != 0', and the Friedmann equation is a first integral of the other two. In the general 1+3 setting this needs omega_a = 0 (Ellis-van Elst p.13), which holds automatically in FLRW.
hypothesis_drift: No hypothesis is dropped on the direction the tree uses. The source's one conditional, 'if Sdot != 0' (Ellis-van Elst p.22), applies only to constraint + continuity => acceleration. The tree uses constraint + acceleration => continuity (permute.py:115-116, 290-297). That direction is a polynomial identity with no division by adot (C3b, C3d); z3 finds no counterexample (C5a unsat, with the vacuity guard C5b sat). A static counterexample shows the condition is needed in the other direction (C4b).
UNITS (permute.py:280, 285-287): 8piG/3 = 1 gives addot = -(1/2)(rho+3p)a, which is exactly _accel (C1g). No drift.
LAMBDA as the w = -1 fluid matches Carroll 8.29-8.31 (C1h). No drift.

EQUATION OF STATE (permute.py:115-117, 445-451): the tree uses constant w, while the source allows p = p(mu). The identity holds for any pressure P (C3c), so the tree's class is narrower than the source's. No drift.

CURVATURE (permute.py:117, 300-303): k = 0 or +/-1/4 with a0 = 1 is a rescaling of Carroll's k in {-1, 0, +1}. The requirement adot0 = sqrt(1-k) > 0 is guarded by the ValueError at permute.py:302-303. No drift.

GR is not listed among the canonical hypotheses, but the owner states it at permute.py:107 ('Couple it to Einstein's equation'). It is named here so it is not lost: minimally coupled matter, Levi-Civita connection, no modified gravity.

On the fixture the worst value is 7.2e-16, and it is 6.0e-16 at 500 steps against 5.9e-16 at 8000. So the RK4 integration does no work, and any integrator would show the same flatness. This is a named qualifier and fits the owner's own words ('AN IDENTITY DOES NOT' shrink). It is not a drift against the tree.

DIRECTION. I redid the algebra by hand: 2H(addot/a - H^2) - 2kH/a^2 + 3H(1+w)rho = H[2rho - 2(H^2 + k/a^2)] = 0. It holds identically and nothing is divided by adot, so the source's 'if Sdot != 0' only constrains the converse direction, which the tree does not use. DATA. No datum enters the identity. DESI's evolving w and the H0 tension change rho(a) and applicability, not the equations.

(2) The tree mislabels w = -2/3 as 'curvature-like'. A term going as k/a^2 has rho ~ a^-3(1+w), which gives w = -1/3. audits.published_statement: Tree (arrival.py:7-9): 'REVERSE SLINGSHOT. The coupling is time-symmetric: a pass with the deflector receding takes back exactly what a head-on pass gave, dv = 2U/(1+U^2) either way.' arrival.py:37: 'dv = 2U/(1+U^2), the strong-field limit. Sign is the encounter geometry.' arrival.py:109-111: 'the same magnitude negative with it receding. Braking is departure run backwards and costs nothing.' External content that could be read: Zhang (2020) p.13 says head-tail encounters decelerate, and that aberration makes head-on encounters statistically commoner. The optimised upper limit is 'a 50% gain [in gamma] when |v_A| = 0.2c'. The Newtonian analogue in Acevedo & Ritz (2026) Eq. (2.10) is Delta eps = u_M2 v_i (cos beta - cos(beta+chi)), 'maximal energy gain is 2 u_M2 v_i, which occurs when beta = 0 and chi = 180 deg'. That formula is 'technically only valid for the restricted 3-body problem, in which the heavy component is effectively at rest and a sufficiently close encounter ... can be described as a two-body hyperbolic scattering event in the rest frame of the secondary'. The exact law re-derived here: a full reversal in the rest frame of a deflector moving at U adds exactly 2 artanh U to the ship's rapidity. From rest this gives v_f = 2U/(1+U^2).
published_hypotheses: Elastic scattering in the deflector's rest frame: the speed at infinity is conserved there. This needs a stationary field in that frame, i.e. an isolated deflector moving uniformly during the encounter (restricted-3-body idealisation; Acevedo & Ritz Sec. 2).
Test particle: the ship's mass is negligible against the deflector's, so recoil is neglected (Acevedo & Ritz p.5).
Maximum gain needs the head-on geometry (beta = 0) and full reversal (chi = 180 deg) (Acevedo & Ritz p.5).
Deflection near pi without striking the body needs a compact deflector, which is the strong-field clause (Zhang abstract, p.1).
The single-encounter formula holds when one hyperbolic encounter describes the event. In compact equal-mass BH binaries ejections exceed it by an order-unity factor (Acevedo & Ritz p.5).
Zhang's 50%-per-pass figure is optimised over the entry phase phi0 and the angular momentum L (Fig. 8, pp.13-14).
Special-relativistic velocity addition between the deflector frame and the lab frame (Einstein 1905; NAMED-NOT-READ; re-derived here).

**The discrepancy is systematic, not a one-equation misprint.**
- Null-contracting (9) with g_ll = 0 gives T_ll = (l.dphi)^2 - xi l l nabla nabla phi^2 + xi R_ll phi^2. Written in (13)'s bracket form, that bracket is phi(l l nabla nabla phi) - 1/2 R_ll phi^2.

- Q[f] in (64) and (69b) has +1/2. This matches none of the paper's own earlier equations: (13) as printed implies +1, (61) as extracted implies +2, and (9) implies -1.
